studies.label: Online experiment with professionals: occupation-specific writing with ChatGPT versus Overleaf signup

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Method, recruitment; PDF p. 18, Table 1; PDF p. 19, Table 1 note
counts_source.quote: we recruited 453 experienced, college-educated professionals on the survey platform Prolific and assigned each to complete two occupation-specific, incentivized writing tasks (21).

arms.name: Treatment (ChatGPT)
arms.description: After the pre-intervention writing task, participants were instructed to register for ChatGPT, received guidance, and could use it on the second task. Assignment was to access and encouragement, with optional use (PDF p. 3, Method).

arms.name: Control (Overleaf signup)
arms.description: Registered for Overleaf to match signup time and hassle, without being told they could use it on the second task. This is the no-assigned-AI control, not an active writing-aid intervention. Some control participants independently used ChatGPT (PDF p. 3, Method; PDF p. 4, Takeup of ChatGPT).

studies.task: Professionals completed occupation-specific writing tasks, including press releases, short reports, analysis plans, and delicate emails, before and after the signup intervention.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Method: GPT-3.5 is named and the experiment is dated January 27 to February 21, 2023; no model release year is stated, so year is null.

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry, https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/10882; DOI 10.1257/rct.10882-2.1 (PDF p. 11, Data and materials availability).

estimates.outcome: Average evaluator grade: pooled main incentive schemes, Figure 1
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Blinded experienced professionals working in the same occupations scored the produced writing on a 1-7 scale; each output was seen by three evaluators. The saved manuscript does not supply a grade-specific rubric or explain the aggregation across grade dimensions. Figure 1B uses participant-evaluator observations of pre-to-post grade changes. Figure 1D prints raw post-treatment grade means at the same participant-evaluator level.

regression.model: Regression of within-participant pre-to-post grade change on treatment, occupation*task-order fixed effects, incentive-arm fixed effects, and grader fixed effects, at the participant-evaluator level, with standard errors clustered by person. The displayed coefficient and interval are rescaled after estimation by the pre-treatment outcome SD. The raw coefficient and its SE are not printed; the rescaled effect is recorded only in paper_effect.

paper_effect.standardizer: Pre-treatment standard deviation of the outcome variable (Figure 1 note). The manuscript does not specify the arm composition or whether this SD is across participant means or individual evaluator ratings; it is not identified as the control-arm participant-level SD.

estimates.notes: Retained as the paper's main pooled analysis across the linear and convex incentive schemes, with all assigned ChatGPT and control participants in that analysis population rather than an ability, occupation, actual-use, or single-incentive cell comparison. It excludes the separate fixed-time incentive group and is not an effect over all recruited participants. The paper reports this pooled main specification and the fixed-time robustness subgroup separately. Raw post-treatment rating means come from Figure 1D. The Figure 1B effect and confidence interval are adjusted grade-change effects rescaled by the pre-treatment outcome SD after estimation. Therefore the rescaled effect is stored as paper_effect.type=other, not as a coefficient from an outcome known to have been standardized before estimation. The confidence interval belongs to that paper effect, not the unadjusted difference between the raw means. The paper does not identify the standardizer as a control-arm or pooled participant-level SD; sd_level remains null. Only printed figure labels are transcribed; arm-mean confidence intervals have no printed endpoints. Person-clustered uncertainty supports se_basis=participant despite unit=rating. The narrative standardized effect is kept separately because its value differs and its sample/model are not separately identified. No paired crossover took place, and no statistics were computed.
estimates.primary_override_reason: Rule 3: The supplied paper does not distinguish these reports of the main average-grade contrast as primary or as the abstract's preferred specification, and the prose record's unspecified model cannot be assumed to be unadjusted. The Figure 1 record alone has accepted data_stats with participant-level arm means, SDs, and counts, permitting a participant-level standardized effect. sources.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract, alternative percentage summary of output quality

estimates.notes: The prose reports an effect in standard-deviation units without naming it Cohen's d, Hedges' g, or a standardized beta, so paper_effect.type is other. It does not separately identify the sample, denominator, analysis unit, or uncertainty model behind this number. The Figure 1 specification and confidence interval are not transferred to this record. The abstract additionally summarizes output quality as an 18% increase; that alternative expression of the same outcome is preserved here, not treated as another independent contrast or converted into a proportion. This is a work-quality outcome, not an overall-creativity rating. No grade-specific effect or p-value is inferred from this average-grade result.

not_extracted.what: Average evaluator grade in the fixed-time incentive subgroup (S1-O1 secondary contrast)
not_extracted.reason: Excluded as an incentive-specific subgroup result under extraction rule 5. The paper reports this separately from the pooled main incentive schemes (PDF p. 4, Productivity; PDF p. 10, note 26). Its model, analysis unit, exact sample counts, and numerical uncertainty are not supplied.

not_extracted.what: Output quality: abstract percentage increase (s1_average_grade_chatgpt_vs_control_abstract_percent; only in B)
not_extracted.reason: The abstract summarizes the same average output-quality treatment-control finding in percentage units; it does not introduce another outcome, arm, or sample contrast. Under the one-contrast-per-outcome-and-sample definition, it is not retained as an additional estimate. Its exact wording is preserved in the sources and notes of s1_average_grade_chatgpt_vs_control_text: "output quality rose by 18%." No conversion or inference about its denominator is made (PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Productivity).

not_extracted.what: Separate linear and convex incentive-scheme results
not_extracted.reason: The paper describes these results as virtually identical but prints no separate grade effect for either scheme; such separate incentive-cell comparisons would be subgroup results under extraction rule 5. The paper's pooled main analysis remains identified explicitly as restricted to these schemes (PDF p. 4, Productivity; PDF p. 12, Figure 1 note).

not_extracted.what: Self-reported task completion time
not_extracted.reason: Productivity/time-use outcome, not creativity or diversity scored on the produced output (PDF p. 4, Productivity; PDF p. 12, Figure 1A and 1C).

not_extracted.reason: Reports participants' choices to edit or replace, not scored quality/originality of the revised output or a full-sample randomized contrast (PDF p. 4, Productivity, final paragraph).

not_extracted.what: Editing behavior, time after pasting, and association between editing time and grade
not_extracted.reason: Descriptive process measures and a non-random association with post-treatment editing behavior, rather than a randomized assistance contrast on output creativity (PDF p. 5, Human-Machine Interactions; PDF p. 10, note 27).

not_extracted.what: Grades of ChatGPT-using participants versus raw ChatGPT output
not_extracted.reason: Raw ChatGPT output is an arm in which no person worked; observed use also conditions on post-treatment compliance. Excluded under extraction rule 5 (PDF p. 5, Human-Machine Interactions).

not_extracted.what: Reasons for not using ChatGPT, task realism, and participants' prior experience with similar tasks
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported perceptions, background characteristics, or barriers, not output-based creativity outcomes (PDF p. 3, Method; PDF p. 6, follow-up surveys).

not_extracted.what: Baseline descriptive and balance comparisons, including first-task grades
not_extracted.reason: Pre-intervention sample descriptions and balance checks, not effects of generative-AI assignment while producing the scored second-task output (PDF pp. 18-19, Table 1 and note).

not_extracted.what: Cross-evaluator correlation of grades
not_extracted.reason: This describes grading reliability, not a treatment-control effect on participants' output quality or diversity (PDF p. 3, Method; PDF p. 10, note 23).

not_extracted.what: Supplement-only Lee bounds, employment/occupation-adjusted robustness results, and two-stage least squares estimates
not_extracted.reason: Referenced on PDF pp. 3-4, but no numerical versions or separate specifications are printed in the saved manuscript. The separate Supplementary Materials are absent from the saved PDF and supplement-manifest.json lists no saved files. These unavailable results are not reconstructed or assigned the main figure's numbers.

open_items: Exact participant counts randomized and analyzed, overall and by arm/outcome, are not explicitly established by a participant flow or post-treatment regression sample count. The recruitment count and Table 1 descriptive/baseline Ns do not establish those quantities. No counts were inferred from proportions, summed cells, or degrees of freedom (PDF p. 3; PDF pp. 18-19).

The main-text standardized average-grade effect differs from Figure 1, and the manuscript does not identify the exact sample/model responsible for the difference. The abstract also gives a percentage summary without its denominator or model. These reports cannot be merged by assigning the figure's interval, sample, or clustering to the prose result (PDF pp. 1, 4, 12-13).

Figure 1 supplies no numerical grade SD, raw adjusted coefficient, or coefficient SE. Its pre-treatment SD standardizer is not identified by arm composition or observation level; do not treat the displayed rescaled effect as a confirmed control-arm or pooled participant-level standardized mean difference (PDF p. 12, Figure 1 note).

Originality, overall grade, writing-quality grade, and content-quality grade lack separately printed numerical effects, uncertainty, analysis units, models, and sample counts. Their relationship to average evaluator grade is not defined. The general evaluator protocol does not establish the observation unit of each separate grade analysis (PDF pp. 3-4).

Supplementary Materials are referenced but not embedded in the saved PDF; the local supplement manifest lists no saved files. The referenced rubrics, additional grade analyses, Lee bounds, baseline-covariate robustness, and compliance-adjusted estimates could not be checked. No supplementary numerical result was inferred.
The manuscript confirms preregistration but does not name a preregistered primary outcome. The preregistration itself was not consulted (PDF p. 11).
Participant country and the model release year are not stated. The experiment dates are not a model release date, and the authors' affiliation is not a participant location (PDF pp. 1, 3).

review_corrections.basis: 'In a preregistered online experiment, we assigned occupation-specific, incentivized writing tasks to 453 college-educated professionals, and randomly exposed half of them to ChatGPT.' (PDF p. 1, abstract; also PDF p. 3). No analyzed total is printed; the posted-data analysis uses 167 and 186 people for the average-grade contrast.
